posted.title: Studying chronic cancer treatment toxicities? Support for R01 projects
Why Even One Outlier Destroys the Mean

points.heading: The Mean Has Zero Breakdown
points.body: The sample mean is defined as the sum of observations divided by n. If any single observation gets arbitrarily large, the mean becomes arbitrarily large. Thus the breakdown point for the mean is 0.

points.heading: The Median Survives Extremes
points.body: The median is the central value in a distribution where equal numbers of values lie above and below. If a minority of observations go to infinity, the median will not be arbitrarily bad. Its breakdown point is one half.

points.heading: When Is the Mean Actually Good?
points.body: Considering stability and breakdown limits, the mean only works well when datasets lack outliers, skewness, and multiple modes. The median is far less affected by these departures from normality.

posted.takeaway: Even a single outlier makes the sample mean completely arbitrary, giving it a breakdown point of zero.

posted.title: Linear or Logistic Regression? Look at Your Outcome

points.heading: The outcome dictates the model
points.body: Regression helps identify how multiple factors connect to disease outcomes. Choosing between linear and logistic models depends directly on how you measure your dependent variable.

points.heading: Linear models require continuous data
points.body: In linear regression, the dependent variable must be continuous, such as intraocular pressure or visual acuity. Independent variables may be continuous, binary, or categorical.

points.heading: Logistic models need binary outcomes
points.body: Logistic regression specifically requires a binary dependent variable, meaning the outcome only has two possible values, such as yes or no.

points.heading: Comparing the effect metrics
points.body: Linear regression reports coefficients showing unit changes in the outcome. Logistic regression expresses predictor effects using an odds ratio to compare relative odds of the event.

posted.takeaway: Linear regression requires a continuous outcome, whereas logistic regression demands a binary dependent variable.

posted.title: Tech transfer and innovation hubs: bridge research results to market
Primary outcome: defined before, not after

points.heading: What the item asks
points.body: Define every pre-specified primary and secondary outcome: the measure, how it was assessed, and exactly when.

points.heading: Why it matters
points.body: Vague outcomes invite switching after the data are in, one of the best-documented sources of reporting bias.

points.heading: How to comply
points.body: Write each outcome as: instrument + metric + aggregation + time point. Example: pain on a 0–10 scale, mean change at 12 weeks.

posted.takeaway: An outcome is pre-specified only if measure, metric and time point are written down first.
